header.name: Site
header.description:
Represents a physical location/campus (plant, distribution center, HQ) where operations, assets, and personnel are logically grouped. Top-level scope for facilities, compliance settings, and region-specific configurations.

**Typical Use Cases**

- Segregate production metrics, inventory, labor, and compliance by location.
- Scope access controls, schedules, and integrations to a physical site.

modelDefinition.name: Site

fields.name: id
fields.description:
**`id`** (`ID!`, unique, queryable, where-enabled, create-included, update-excluded)
 **What it is:** The immutable, primary unique identifier for a Site record.
 **Behavior:**

- Returned in queries and usable in `where` filters.
- Included on create; not updatable once persisted.
 **Examples:** `"c3f1b3c0-8b3d-4b2b-9e3d-2f9e5b6a12cd"`
 **Notes:** Every model must include an `id`. This key is used in relations (e.g., Areas reference Site via `siteId`).

fields.name: code
fields.description:
**`code`** (`String!`, unique, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** The human-friendly, unique label for the site, used as the main display (`labelField`) and common key in integrations.
 **Behavior:**

- Must be unique per tenant.
- Required at creation; can be updated (ensure downstream references are resilient).
 **Examples:** `DET-PLANT01`, `MX-GDL-DC1`
 **Recommended Pattern:** `[COUNTRY/REGION]-[CITY]-[FACILITY]` (e.g., `US-DET-PLT1`).

fields.name: isActive
fields.description:
**`isActive`** (`Boolean!`, default `true`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Operational flag indicating whether the site is active for scheduling, telemetry, and reporting.
 **Behavior:**

- Defaults to `true` on creation.
- When `false`, new scheduling/jobs should be blocked; historical data remains accessible.
 **Examples:** `true` (operational), `false` (paused/archived).

fields.name: city
fields.description:
**`city`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** City or municipality.
 **Examples:** `Detroit`.

fields.name: country
fields.description:
**`country`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Country name or code.
 **Examples:** `USA`, `US`, `Mexico`, `MX`.
 **Recommendation:** Normalize to ISO-3166 alpha-2 (e.g., `US`, `MX`) and keep a display mapping.

fields.name: industry
fields.description:
**`industry`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Industry classification for the site’s operations.
 **Examples:** `Automotive`, `Food & Beverage`, `Aerospace`, `Pharma`.
 **Usage:** Useful for reporting, filtering, and applying templates/policies.

fields.name: name
fields.description:
**`name`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** The formal or long name of the site.
 **Usage:** For display purposes, documentation, and reporting.
 **Examples:** `Detroit Plant 1`, `Guadalajara Distribution Center`.

fields.name: postalCode
fields.description:
**`postalCode`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Postal or ZIP code.
 **Examples:** `48201`, `44940`.
 **Validation:** Optional format checks per country.

fields.name: state
fields.description:
**`state`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** State/province/region (use ISO whenever possible).
 **Examples:** `MI`, `Jalisco`.
 **Note:** Consider normalizing to ISO-3166-2 codes in validation logic.

fields.name: street
fields.description:
**`street`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Street address line for logistics and compliance.
 **Examples:** `1234 Industrial Way`.

fields.name: timezone
fields.description:
**`timezone`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** IANA timezone identifier used for job windows, OEE, and event timestamps.
 **Examples:** `America/Detroit`, `America/Mexico_City`.
 **Validation:** Ensure valid IANA TZ (e.g., via library or known list); this drives scheduling behavior.

*Note - you might use the tenant timezone setting instead - if ONLY supporting single site within the app.

fields.name: type
fields.description:
**`type`** (`String`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Classification of the site.
 **Common Values:** `Plant`, `DistributionCenter`, `Headquarters`, `R&D`, `VendorManaged`.
 **Notes:** Use consistent enumerations in your app logic even though stored as string.

fields.name: areas
fields.description:
**`areas`** (`[Area!]!`, relation via `Site.id → Area.siteId`, queryable, where-enabled, create/update-included)
 **What it is:** Collection of Areas associated to the Site.
 **Behavior:**

- Populated through relation: `from: "id"` (Site) to `to: "siteId"` (Area).
- Included in create/update inputs to allow nested operations if your mutation handlers support it.
 **Notes:** Typical hierarchy is **Site → Area → Line → Cell**; enforce referential integrity in mutations.
